To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nuclear magnetic moments of the stable isotopes of the alkali elements Li, Na andK, measured with an accuracy of 10−8 or better, are consistent with the values of the nuclear moments calculated from the shell model of nuclear structure.
we measured the magnetic moments of the stable isotopes6Li,7Lii,23Na, 39K and 41K in the 2S1/22 ground state and the hyperfine constants in the 2P3/22 ground state.
the nuclear magnetic moment of6Li in the2S12S1/2- ground state isgI/gJ=1.22156978(10).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the magnetic properties of the stable alkalis.
the measurement of the magnetic dipole moments and the hyperfine structure constants of the stable alkalis in the ground state.
the determination of the nuclear magnetic moments of stable isotopes of Li, Na andK.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the atomic beam magnetic dipole moment technique is the method of choice for the measurement ofgI- andΔν-values of stable and long living isotopes.
the atomic beam magnetic resonances are more precise than the NMR-methods.
all the measurements are in excellent agreement with the most precise results obtained so far by the NMR method, but with a precision of the order of 10−4 or better.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absolutegI- andgJ-factors of the stable isotopes Li, Li, Na and the isotopes K, K in the2D5/2-ground states can be calculated from the present results.
we have determined the nuclear magnetic moments of the stable isotopes of the alkali atoms in their 2S1/ 2-ground states with an accuracy of about 3 parts in 10−6.
we have measured all the nuclear magnetic dipolar moments of the stable isotopes of the alkali metals in the2S12-ground state with an accuracy better than 0.01 ppm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemical shifts of 23Na and 39K in the NMR-solvent D2O and H2O are very similar, but differ from the chemical shift of 41K.
the NMR method is very sensitive to the chemical shifts of NMR frequencies.
the magnetic dipole moment of the nucleus is not a fundamental property, but rather depends on the environment.
